description: Baseline spends 73.8% of GPU time in the unblocked scalar Householder panel kernel (no tensor cores) on the dominant batch640-n512 / batch60-n1024 shapes. Replace it with RECURSIVE blocked Householder QR (Elmroth-Gustavson): factor a narrow panel with a custom CUDA C++ kernel (panel in shared memory), recurse to halve panel width, build the block reflector T, and apply the WY update (I - V T V^T)^T to the trailing submatrix as large cublasGemmStridedBatched / cublasGemmEx calls so the bulk of FLOPs run on tensor cores. Emit compact (H,tau) reflectors natively. Tune panel width nb; route n off the supported grid to a torch.geqrf fallback (off-grid-n guard).

Attack the same 73.8% scalar-panel bottleneck with a normal-equations path that is almost pure tensor-core GEMM: G = A^T A (batched cublas SYRK/GEMM), R = Cholesky(G) (custom batched CUDA C++ Cholesky or cuSOLVER potrfBatched), Q = A R^{-1} (batched TRSM), then reconstruct compact Householder (H,tau) from the orthonormal Q via the LAPACK orhr_col algorithm so output matches the geqrf contract exactly (watch the diagonal sign convention so householder_product(H,tau) reproduces Q). Robustness is the hard part and is gated: ill-conditioned rankdef/clustered/nearrank/mixed cases must be correct ON THEIR OWN MERITS (functional-invariance guard forbids content-dispatch). Use shifted CholeskyQR2/CholeskyQR3 with a breakdown fallback to Householder; FP32 factors out.

On large batches of small/medium matrices (batch20-n32, batch40-n176, batch40-n352, and the n<=256 tiles) the baseline is launch/latency bound: many tiny per-matrix kernels plus global-memory round-trips. Write a custom CUDA C++ batched QR that assigns ONE CTA per matrix and keeps the whole matrix on-chip (shared memory + registers), running the full Householder factorization without inter-kernel global round-trips; use CUB block primitives for in-CTA column-norm and dot-product reductions, and emit compact (H,tau) directly. Pin this on-chip path to n<=256 (n=512 FP32 is 1MB, exceeds shared memory); route n>256 and off-grid n to a correct fallback (torch.geqrf) so the off-grid-n guard passes. Try multiple-matrices-per-CTA for the tiniest n to cut launch overhead further.

Your n=32/176 register-resident kernels are latency-bound on an UNDERFILLED grid: batch=40 launches only 40 CTAs for 188 SMs (0.21 waves, ~11% SM throughput) — that, not coverage, is the bottleneck. Attack grid-fill on the shapes you already factor correctly (n=32, n=176): use a persistent-kernel / multiple-matrices-per-CTA scheme so all 188 SMs are busy, and lower TPC to raise CTAs-per-SM and resident warps. (Your earlier MPC=4 n=32 attempt was a narrow warp-per-matrix variant; this is broader — persistent CTAs looping the batch, occupancy-driven.) Profile with ncu to confirm waves/SM and achieved occupancy rise. Keep correctness + all guards; route n>256 and off-grid n to geqrf. Do NOT attempt n=352 register-resident (352^2*4=484KB exceeds the register file).

You hit 11.49x on big-batch n=512/1024 but only 1.72x on n=2048 (batch8) and 1.0x on n=4096 (batch2, still geqrf) — the geomean's center of gravity now (fixing both is ~1.4x geomean, vs ~1.07x from polishing the fast shapes). Your blocked kernel is at its FP32 floor; n=2048 (1.72x) and n=4096 (geqrf, 1.0x) stayed unfixable ONLY because the 100KB shared cap forces tiny nb. TSQR (communication-avoiding QR) is the Householder-lane fix and keeps you DISTINCT from workers 1/2 (normal-equations CholeskyQR): the panel is tall-skinny (m x nb), so split its HEIGHT across many CTAs -- each CTA does a short tall-skinny Householder on a row-block (a LARGER nb now fits in shared), then a Householder reduction tree merges the per-block R's. This fills the 188 SMs (batch 2-8 -> many CTAs/matrix) AND enables large nb. TSQR is unconditionally backward-stable, so UNLIKE worker 2's CholeskyQR-n=4096 (which falls back to geqrf at 1.0x on the ill-conditioned cases) it needs NO robustness fallback -- and since the benchmark RANKS conditioning robustness, TSQR is the only path that can beat 1.0x on ill-conditioned n=4096. PRIMARY target n=2048 (you own it, ~1.72x->~3x is +4.7% geomean alone); n=4096 as stretch/hedge. CRITICAL RISK + GUARDRAIL: a TSQR tree yields a FACTORED Q, not flat compact (H,tau); reconstructing the single geqrf-compatible (H,tau) (orhr_col-style, proven in this run) can cost as much as the factorization. So in iteration 0-1 MEASURE the reconstruction cost IN ISOLATION first; if reconstruction is >= the factorization it replaces, ABANDON TSQR and instead do RECURSIVE blocked Householder (Elmroth-Gustavson): recurse the panel (factor left half, WY-update right half, factor right half) so the on-chip working set is a sub-panel not full n x nb, growing effective nb at n=2048/4096 without the 100KB cap -- this stays in the Householder lane AND emits compact (H,tau) NATIVELY (no reconstruction). Keep all other dispatch branches unchanged; FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards green; profile to confirm SMs-in-use and nb both rise on n=2048/4096.
